{"Write":"C:\\TU\\Projects\\Agentic-Hackathon-Munich-EHL-Team-Harissa-\\autoimplants\\mesh_quality.py: \"\"\"Quality gate for a bone mesh arriving from outside this repo.\n\n``inputs/bone.stl`` is generated by ``inputs/make_bone.py``, so it is watertight,\nsingle-component, in millimetres and a few thousand triangles by construction. A\nreal CT-derived mesh is none of those things by construction: segmentation leaves\nislands of speckle, marching cubes emits hundreds of thousands of triangles, and\nwhether the file is in millimetres depends on which tool wrote it.\n\nEvery one of those failures is silent downstream. A stray island shifts the mesh\nbounds and moves every ray launch point; a metres-scale mesh passes every\nthreshold trivially because a 1.5 mm gap limit against a 0.4 mm-long femur is\nmeaningless. So the gate runs before a real case is accepted, and it reports in\nthe same ``Report``/``Check`` shape as the validators -- one report format for\nthe whole project.\n\nThe gate is advisory about repairs it can make (islands, holes, triangle count)\nand hard about the ones it cannot (empty, unreadable, wrong scale).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom .contracts import FAIL, PASS, Check, Report\n\n# Expected largest dimension of a whole bone, in mm. Used only to catch a mesh\n# written in metres or centimetres -- these are sanity bounds, not morphometry.\nBONE_EXTENT_MM = {\n    \"femur\": (250.0, 600.0),\n    \"tibia\": (250.0, 520.0),\n    \"fibula\": (250.0, 500.0),\n    \"humerus\": (200.0, 450.0),\n    \"radius\": (150.0, 350.0),\n    \"ulna\": (150.0, 350.0),\n}\n_GENERIC_EXTENT_MM = (20.0, 1200.0)\n\n# Above this, ray casting and containment queries dominate the validator runtime.\n# A decimated femur is still far finer than the gap thresholds being measured.\nMAX_FACES = 200_000\n\n# An island smaller than this fraction of the largest component is segmentation\n# speckle, not anatomy.\nISLAND_FRACTION = 0.05\n\nUNIT_SCALE_MM = {\"mm\": 1.0, \"cm\": 10.0, \"m\": 1000.0}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass MeshGateResult:\n    \"\"\"What the gate decided, plus the cleaned mesh if it could produce one.\"\"\"\n\n    report: Report\n    mesh: object | None = None\n    repairs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n    @property\n    def passed(self) -> bool:\n        return self.report.passed\n\n\ndef load_mesh(path: str | Path):\n    \"\"\"Load any mesh trimesh can read, as a single concatenated Trimesh.\"\"\"\n    import trimesh\n\n    mesh = trimesh.load(str(path), force=\"mesh\")\n    if mesh.is_empty or len(mesh.faces) == 0:\n        raise ValueError(f\"mesh at {path} is empty or unreadable\")\n    return mesh\n\n\ndef _check_readable(mesh) -> Check:\n    n = int(len(mesh.faces))\n    return Check(\n        id=\"mesh_non_empty\",\n        status=PASS if n > 0 else FAIL,\n        value=float(n),\n        limit=1.0,\n        unit=\"faces\",\n        message=f\"mesh carries {n} triangles\",\n    )\n\n\ndef _check_units(mesh, bone: str, unit_scale: float) -> Check:\n    extent = float(np.max(mesh.bounds[1] - mesh.bounds[0]))\n    lo, hi = BONE_EXTENT_MM.get(bone, _GENERIC_EXTENT_MM)\n    ok = lo <= extent <= hi\n\n    hint = \"\"\n    if not ok:\n        for name, scale in UNIT_SCALE_MM.items():\n            if lo <= extent * scale <= hi:\n                hint = (\n                    f\" -- the extent is plausible if the file is in {name}; \"\n                    f\"re-run with --units {name}\"\n                )\n                break\n\n    return Check(\n        id=\"mesh_units_plausible\",\n        status=PASS if ok else FAIL,\n        value=round(extent, 2),\n        limit=hi,\n        unit=\"mm\",\n        message=(\n            f\"largest dimension {extent:.0f} mm is a plausible {bone} \"\n            f\"(expected {lo:.0f}-{hi:.0f} mm, unit scale x{unit_scale:g})\"\n            if ok\n            else f\"largest dimension is {extent:.1f} mm, outside the {lo:.0f}-{hi:.0f} mm \"\n                 f\"expected for a {bone}. Every threshold in the case is in mm, so a \"\n                 f\"mesh at the wrong scale passes or fails them meaninglessly{hint}\"\n        ),\n    )\n\n\ndef _check_components(mesh, repairs: list[str]):\n    \"\"\"Split off segmentation speckle, keep the bone.\"\"\"\n    parts = mesh.split(only_watertight=False)\n    if len(parts) <= 1:\n        return mesh, Check(\n            id=\"mesh_single_component\",\n            status=PASS,\n            value=1.0,\n            limit=1.0,\n            unit=\"count\",\n            message=\"mesh is a single connected component\",\n        )\n\n    sizes = np.array([len(p.faces) for p in parts], dtype=float)\n    order = np.argsort(sizes)[::-1]\n    biggest = parts[order[0]]\n    kept_fraction = sizes[order[0]] / sizes.sum()\n    islands = int(len(parts) - 1)\n    big_islands = int((sizes[order[1:]] > ISLAND_FRACTION * sizes[order[0]]).sum())\n\n    if big_islands:\n        # Two comparable components is not speckle -- it is a second bone in the\n        # field of view, or a segmentation that split the shaft. A human has to\n        # look at that, so it fails rather than silently picking the larger one.\n        return mesh, Check(\n            id=\"mesh_single_component\",\n            status=FAIL,\n            value=float(len(parts)),\n            limit=1.0,\n            unit=\"count\",\n            message=f\"mesh has {big_islands} component(s) comparable in size to the \"\n                    f\"largest -- the segmentation may include a second bone or have \"\n                    f\"split the shaft. Review the segmentation before importing\",\n        )\n\n    repairs.append(f\"dropped {islands} speckle island(s), kept {kept_fraction:.1%} of faces\")\n    return biggest, Check(\n        id=\"mesh_single_component\",\n        status=PASS,\n        value=float(len(parts)),\n        limit=1.0,\n        unit=\"count\",\n        message=f\"kept the largest of {len(parts)} components ({kept_fraction:.1%} of \"\n                f\"faces); {islands} speckle island(s) removed\",\n    )\n\n\ndef _check_watertight(mesh, repairs: list[str]):\n    \"\"\"Try to close the mesh. Containment queries are undefined on an open surface.\"\"\"\n    if mesh.is_watertight:\n        return mesh, Check(\n            id=\"mesh_watertight\",\n            status=PASS,\n            value=1.0,\n            limit=1.0,\n            unit=\"bool\",\n            message=\"mesh is closed\",\n        )\n\n    repaired = mesh.copy()\n    repaired.remove_unreferenced_vertices()\n    repaired.update_faces(repaired.nondegenerate_faces())\n    repaired.fill_holes()\n    repaired.fix_normals()\n\n    if repaired.is_watertight:\n        repairs.append(\"filled holes to close the mesh\")\n        return repaired, Check(\n            id=\"mesh_watertight\",\n            status=PASS,\n            value=1.0,\n            limit=1.0,\n            unit=\"bool\",\n            message=\"mesh was open and was repaired to watertight\",\n        )\n\n    return repaired, Check(\n        id=\"mesh_watertight\",\n        status=FAIL,\n        value=0.0,\n        limit=1.0,\n        unit=\"bool\",\n        message=\"mesh is not watertight and hole filling did not close it. \"\n                \"bone.contains() and the gap checks need a closed surface, so the \"\n                \"segmentation has to be cleaned before import\",\n    )\n\n\ndef _check_face_budget(mesh, repairs: list[str], max_faces: int):\n    n = int(len(mesh.faces))\n    if n <= max_faces:\n        return mesh, Check(\n            id=\"mesh_face_budget\",\n            status=PASS,\n            value=float(n),\n            limit=float(max_faces),\n            unit=\"faces\",\n            message=\"triangle count is within the ray-casting budget\",\n        )\n\n    try:\n        reduced = mesh.simplify_quadric_decimation(face_count=max_faces)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        return mesh, Check(\n            id=\"mesh_face_budget\",\n            status=PASS,\n            value=float(n),\n            limit=float(max_faces),\n            unit=\"faces\",\n            message=f\"{n} triangles exceeds the {max_faces} budget and decimation is \"\n                    f\"unavailable ({exc!r}); validation will run but slowly. \"\n                    f\"pip install fast-simplification to enable decimation\",\n        )\n\n    repairs.append(f\"decimated {n} faces to {len(reduced.faces)}\")\n    return reduced, Check(\n        id=\"mesh_face_budget\",\n        status=PASS,\n        value=float(len(reduced.faces)),\n        limit=float(max_faces),\n        unit=\"faces\",\n        message=f\"decimated from {n} triangles to fit the ray-casting budget\",\n    )\n\n\ndef gate(\n    path: str | Path,\n    bone: str = \"femur\",\n    units: str = \"mm\",\n    max_faces: int = MAX_FACES,\n) -> MeshGateResult:\n    \"\"\"Run every mesh check, returning the cleaned mesh when it can be salvaged.\"\"\"\n    repairs: list[str] = []\n\n    try:\n        mesh = load_mesh(path)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        return MeshGateResult(report=Report.errored(\"mesh_readable\", str(exc)))\n\n    scale = UNIT_SCALE_MM.get(units)\n    if scale is None:\n        return MeshGateResult(\n            report=Report.errored(\n                \"mesh_units\", f\"unknown units {units!r}, expected one of {sorted(UNIT_SCALE_MM)}\"\n            )\n        )\n    if scale != 1.0:\n        mesh = mesh.copy()\n        mesh.apply_scale(scale)\n        repairs.append(f\"scaled from {units} to mm (x{scale:g})\")\n\n    checks = [_check_readable(mesh), _check_units(mesh, bone, scale)]\n\n    mesh, c = _check_components(mesh, repairs)\n    checks.append(c)\n    mesh, c = _check_watertight(mesh, repairs)\n    checks.append(c)\n    mesh, c = _check_face_budget(mesh, repairs, max_faces)\n    checks.append(c)\n\n    report = Report.from_checks(\n        checks,\n        meta={\n            \"validator\": \"mesh_quality\",\n            \"source\": str(path),\n            \"repairs\": repairs,\n            \"faces\": int(len(mesh.faces)),\n        },\n    )\n    return MeshGateResult(report=report, mesh=mesh if report.passed else None, repairs=repairs)\n"}
{"Write":"C:\\TU\\Projects\\Agentic-Hackathon-Munich-EHL-Team-Harissa-\\autoimplants\\surgical_plan.py: \"\"\"The schema for externally supplied surgical planning data, and its checks.\n\nSurgical planning -- segmentation, screw placement, keepout definition, load\nestimation -- is a declared PRE-SOLVED input for this project. That decision is\nwhat makes the scope honest: this repo designs an implant around a plan, it does\nnot decide where to put screws in a patient. So a real case arrives as a mesh\nplus a plan, and this module's job is to refuse a plan it cannot design against\nrather than to invent the missing half.\n\nNothing here guesses. A missing landmark, an unnormalisable screw direction or a\nfootprint that runs off the end of the shaft is an error with a message naming\nthe field, never a default that quietly produces a plausible-looking implant.\n\nCoordinate frames\n-----------------\nA plan is written in whatever frame the planning software used -- usually CT\nscanner coordinates, with the origin at the scanner isocentre and no relation to\nthe bone. Everything downstream of here assumes the repo frame:\n\n    +Z  along the shaft, proximal to distal, origin at the proximal landmark\n    +X  the aspect the plate mounts on\n    +Y  the plate width direction\n\n:func:`frame_transform` builds the rigid transform between the two from the\nlandmarks in the plan. The mesh, the screws and the keepouts all go through the\nsame transform, so their relative geometry is untouched -- this is a change of\ndescription, not of anatomy.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom .contracts import FAIL, PASS, Check, Report\n\nREQUIRED_FIELDS = (\n    \"case_id\",\n    \"bone\",\n    \"side\",\n    \"approach\",\n    \"coordinate_frame\",\n    \"footprint_z_mm\",\n    \"screws\",\n    \"keepouts\",\n    \"material\",\n    \"thresholds\",\n)\n\nREQUIRED_SCREW_FIELDS = (\"id\", \"entry_mm\", \"direction\", \"diameter_mm\", \"length_mm\")\n\nREQUIRED_MATERIAL_FIELDS = (\"name\", \"density_g_cm3\")\n\n# Landmark names for the fallback (landmark-based) frame definition.\nLANDMARK_PROXIMAL = \"proximal_shaft_mm\"\nLANDMARK_DISTAL = \"distal_shaft_mm\"\nLANDMARK_LATERAL = \"mount_side_mm\"\n\n# A screw entry is planning data, so it should sit on the bone surface. This is\n# the slack allowed for segmentation and rounding, not for a misplaced screw.\nENTRY_TOLERANCE_MM = 2.5\n# Below this the two shaft landmarks are too close to define an axis stably.\nMIN_SHAFT_SPAN_MM = 50.0\n# Below this the mount-side landmark is too near the shaft axis to say which way\n# is out.\nMIN_LATERAL_OFFSET_MM = 5.0\n\n\nclass PlanError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"A surgical plan that cannot be designed against. Always names the field.\"\"\"\n\n\n# -- loading and structural validation ----------------------------------------\n\n\ndef load_plan(path: str | Path) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Read and structurally validate a surgical plan. Raises PlanError.\"\"\"\n    p = Path(path)\n    if not p.exists():\n        raise PlanError(f\"surgical plan not found: {p}\")\n    try:\n        plan = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:\n        raise PlanError(f\"surgical plan {p} is not valid JSON: {exc}\") from exc\n\n    validate_structure(plan)\n    plan[\"_plan_path\"] = str(p.resolve())\n    return plan\n\n\ndef validate_structure(plan: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Every required field present and the right shape. Raises PlanError.\"\"\"\n    missing = [f for f in REQUIRED_FIELDS if f not in plan]\n    if missing:\n        raise PlanError(\n            \"surgical plan is missing required field(s): \"\n            + \", \".join(missing)\n            + \". Surgical planning is a pre-solved input -- this repo will not \"\n              \"invent clinical decisions to fill them in.\"\n        )\n\n    footprint = plan[\"footprint_z_mm\"]\n    if not (isinstance(footprint, (list, tuple)) and len(footprint) == 2):\n        raise PlanError(\"footprint_z_mm must be [z_start, z_end] in mm\")\n    if float(footprint[1]) <= float(footprint[0]):\n        raise PlanError(\n            f\"footprint_z_mm must increase: got {footprint[0]} to {footprint[1]}\"\n        )\n\n    if not plan[\"screws\"]:\n        raise PlanError(\"surgical plan lists no screws; the implant has nothing to fix to\")\n\n    seen_ids = set()\n    for i, s in enumerate(plan[\"screws\"]):\n        missing = [f for f in REQUIRED_SCREW_FIELDS if f not in s]\n        if missing:\n            raise PlanError(f\"screws[{i}] is missing: {', '.join(missing)}\")\n        if s[\"id\"] in seen_ids:\n            raise PlanError(f\"duplicate screw id {s['id']!r}\")\n        seen_ids.add(s[\"id\"])\n\n        entry = np.asarray(s[\"entry_mm\"], dtype=float)\n        if entry.shape != (3,) or not np.isfinite(entry).all():\n            raise PlanError(f\"screws[{i}].entry_mm must be three finite numbers in mm\")\n\n        d = np.asarray(s[\"direction\"], dtype=float)\n        if d.shape != (3,) or not np.isfinite(d).all():\n            raise PlanError(f\"screws[{i}].direction must be three finite numbers\")\n        if float(np.linalg.norm(d)) < 1e-6:\n            raise PlanError(f\"screws[{i}].direction is zero-length and has no trajectory\")\n\n        if float(s[\"diameter_mm\"]) <= 0 or float(s[\"length_mm\"]) <= 0:\n            raise PlanError(f\"screws[{i}] diameter_mm and length_mm must be positive mm\")\n\n    for i, z in enumerate(plan[\"keepouts\"]):\n        if z.get(\"type\") != \"sphere\":\n            raise PlanError(\n                f\"keepouts[{i}].type={z.get('type')!r}; only 'sphere' zones are \"\n                f\"understood by the geometry validator today\"\n            )\n        for f in (\"id\", \"center_mm\", \"radius_mm\"):\n            if f not in z:\n                raise PlanError(f\"keepouts[{i}] is missing {f}\")\n        center = np.asarray(z[\"center_mm\"], dtype=float)\n        if center.shape != (3,) or not np.isfinite(center).all():\n            raise PlanError(f\"keepouts[{i}].center_mm must be three finite numbers in mm\")\n        if float(z[\"radius_mm\"]) <= 0:\n            raise PlanError(f\"keepouts[{i}].radius_mm must be a positive length in mm\")\n\n    missing = [f for f in REQUIRED_MATERIAL_FIELDS if f not in plan[\"material\"]]\n    if missing:\n        raise PlanError(f\"material is missing: {', '.join(missing)}\")\n\n    validate_frame_fields(plan[\"coordinate_frame\"])\n\n\ndef validate_frame_fields(frame: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The frame must be stated, one way or the other. Raises PlanError.\"\"\"\n    if \"axes\" in frame:\n        axes = frame[\"axes\"]\n        for f in (\"shaft\", \"mount_side\", \"origin_mm\"):\n            if f not in axes:\n                raise PlanError(f\"coordinate_frame.axes is missing {f}\")\n        return\n\n    if \"landmarks\" not in frame:\n        raise PlanError(\n            \"coordinate_frame needs either 'landmarks' \"\n            f\"({LANDMARK_PROXIMAL}, {LANDMARK_DISTAL}, {LANDMARK_LATERAL}) \"\n            \"or explicit 'axes' (shaft, mount_side, origin_mm). Without one of \"\n            \"them the mesh orientation is unknown and every measurement in this \"\n            \"repo -- gap, standoff, wall thickness -- is measured along the wrong \"\n            \"direction.\"\n        )\n\n    landmarks = frame[\"landmarks\"]\n    missing = [\n        n for n in (LANDMARK_PROXIMAL, LANDMARK_DISTAL, LANDMARK_LATERAL)\n        if n not in landmarks\n    ]\n    if missing:\n        raise PlanError(f\"coordinate_frame.landmarks is missing: {', '.join(missing)}\")\n\n\n# -- the frame transform ------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef frame_transform(plan: dict) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"4x4 rigid transform from the plan's own frame into the repo frame.\n\n    Rejecting a mesh that is not already axis-aligned would make real CT support\n    useless -- no scanner produces one. So the frame is computed and applied\n    instead: rotation from the stated shaft and mount-side directions,\n    translation putting the proximal landmark at the origin.\n    \"\"\"\n    frame = plan[\"coordinate_frame\"]\n\n    if \"axes\" in frame:\n        shaft = np.asarray(frame[\"axes\"][\"shaft\"], dtype=float)\n        lateral = np.asarray(frame[\"axes\"][\"mount_side\"], dtype=float)\n        origin = np.asarray(frame[\"axes\"][\"origin_mm\"], dtype=float)\n        span = float(np.linalg.norm(shaft))\n        if span < 1e-6:\n            raise PlanError(\"coordinate_frame.axes.shaft is zero-length\")\n    else:\n        lm = frame[\"landmarks\"]\n        proximal = np.asarray(lm[LANDMARK_PROXIMAL], dtype=float)\n        distal = np.asarray(lm[LANDMARK_DISTAL], dtype=float)\n        mount = np.asarray(lm[LANDMARK_LATERAL], dtype=float)\n\n        shaft = distal - proximal\n        span = float(np.linalg.norm(shaft))\n        if span < MIN_SHAFT_SPAN_MM:\n            raise PlanError(\n                f\"{LANDMARK_PROXIMAL} and {LANDMARK_DISTAL} are {span:.1f} mm apart, \"\n                f\"under the {MIN_SHAFT_SPAN_MM:.0f} mm needed to define the shaft axis \"\n                f\"stably. Place them at opposite ends of the diaphysis.\"\n            )\n        lateral = mount - proximal\n        origin = proximal\n\n    z_hat = shaft / np.linalg.norm(shaft)\n\n    # Only the component of the mount-side direction perpendicular to the shaft\n    # carries information about which way is out.\n    lateral_perp = lateral - np.dot(lateral, z_hat) * z_hat\n    offset = float(np.linalg.norm(lateral_perp))\n    if offset < MIN_LATERAL_OFFSET_MM:\n        raise PlanError(\n            f\"the mount-side direction is only {offset:.2f} mm off the shaft axis, \"\n            f\"under the {MIN_LATERAL_OFFSET_MM:.0f} mm minimum -- which way the plate \"\n            f\"faces is ambiguous. Put {LANDMARK_LATERAL} on the aspect the plate \"\n            f\"mounts on, well clear of the axis.\"\n        )\n    x_hat = lateral_perp / offset\n    y_hat = np.cross(z_hat, x_hat)\n\n    rotation = np.vstack([x_hat, y_hat, z_hat])  # rows: source -> repo components\n\n    transform = np.eye(4)\n    transform[:3, :3] = rotation\n    transform[:3, 3] = -rotation @ origin\n    return transform\n\n\ndef transform_points(points: np.ndarray, transform: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Apply a 4x4 rigid transform to an (n, 3) array of positions.\"\"\"\n    pts = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(points, dtype=float))\n    return pts @ transform[:3, :3].T + transform[:3, 3]\n\n\ndef transform_directions(dirs: np.ndarray, transform: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Rotate directions -- no translation, and renormalised.\"\"\"\n    vecs = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(dirs, dtype=float)) @ transform[:3, :3].T\n    norms = np.linalg.norm(vecs, axis=1, keepdims=True)\n    return vecs / norms\n\n\ndef transformed_plan(plan: dict, transform: np.ndarray) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"A copy of the plan with every position and direction in the repo frame.\"\"\"\n    out = dict(plan)\n\n    screws = []\n    for s in plan[\"screws\"]:\n        s = dict(s)\n        s[\"entry_mm\"] = transform_points(s[\"entry_mm\"], transform)[0].tolist()\n        s[\"direction\"] = transform_directions(s[\"direction\"], transform)[0].tolist()\n        screws.append(s)\n    out[\"screws\"] = screws\n\n    keepouts = []\n    for z in plan[\"keepouts\"]:\n        z = dict(z)\n        z[\"center_mm\"] = transform_points(z[\"center_mm\"], transform)[0].tolist()\n        keepouts.append(z)\n    out[\"keepouts\"] = keepouts\n\n    return out\n\n\n# -- planning data against the actual bone ------------------------------------\n\n\ndef validate_against_bone(plan: dict, bone_mesh) -> Report:\n    \"\"\"Check the transformed plan describes screws and zones on *this* bone.\n\n    A plan can be structurally perfect and still refer to a different scan. These\n    checks are what catch a mismatched mesh/plan pair before the design loop\n    spends eight iterations on geometry that was never seated on the bone.\n    \"\"\"\n    checks: list[Check] = []\n    entries = np.array([s[\"entry_mm\"] for s in plan[\"screws\"]], dtype=float)\n    dirs = np.array([s[\"direction\"] for s in plan[\"screws\"]], dtype=float)\n\n    # 1. Entries sit on the bone surface.\n    _, dist, _ = bone_mesh.nearest.on_surface(entries)\n    worst = int(np.argmax(dist))\n    ok = bool(np.all(dist <= ENTRY_TOLERANCE_MM))\n    checks.append(\n        Check(\n            id=\"plan_screw_entries_on_bone\",\n            status=PASS if ok else FAIL,\n            value=round(float(dist[worst]), 3),\n            limit=ENTRY_TOLERANCE_MM,\n            unit=\"mm\",\n            location=[round(float(c), 3) for c in entries[worst]],\n            message=(\n                \"every planned screw entry lies on the bone surface\"\n                if ok\n                else f\"screw {plan['screws'][worst]['id']!r} enters \"\n                     f\"{float(dist[worst]):.1f} mm from the bone surface -- the plan and \"\n                     f\"the mesh may come from different scans, or the landmarks are wrong\"\n            ),\n        )\n    )\n\n    # 2. Each trajectory actually passes through bone, with enough purchase to hold.\n    short = []\n    worst_purchase = float(\"inf\")\n    worst_id = None\n    for s, entry, d in zip(plan[\"screws\"], entries, dirs):\n        origin = entry - d * 1.0  # start just outside so the entry face is hit\n        hits, _, _ = bone_mesh.ray.intersects_location(\n            ray_origins=np.array([origin]), ray_directions=np.array([d])\n        )\n        purchase = 0.0\n        if len(hits) >= 2:\n            along = (hits - origin) @ d\n            purchase = float(np.max(along) - np.min(along))\n        elif len(hits) == 1:\n            purchase = 0.0\n        if purchase < worst_purchase:\n            worst_purchase, worst_id = purchase, s[\"id\"]\n        if purchase <= 0.0:\n            short.append(s[\"id\"])\n\n    checks.append(\n        Check(\n            id=\"plan_screw_trajectories_in_bone\",\n            status=PASS if not short else FAIL,\n            value=round(worst_purchase if np.isfinite(worst_purchase) else 0.0, 3),\n            limit=0.0,\n            unit=\"mm\",\n            message=(\n                f\"every trajectory passes through bone; thinnest purchase is \"\n                f\"{worst_purchase:.1f} mm at {worst_id!r}\"\n                if not short\n                else f\"screw(s) {', '.join(short)} do not pass through the bone along \"\n                     f\"their stated direction -- a screw that misses the bone fixes nothing\"\n            ),\n        )\n    )\n\n    # 3. Footprint lies on the shaft that exists in this mesh.\n    z0, z1 = (float(v) for v in plan[\"footprint_z_mm\"])\n    bone_z0, bone_z1 = float(bone_mesh.bounds[0][2]), float(bone_mesh.bounds[1][2])\n    inside = bone_z0 <= z0 and z1 <= bone_z1\n    checks.append(\n        Check(\n            id=\"plan_footprint_within_bone\",\n            status=PASS if inside else FAIL,\n            value=round(z1 - z0, 2),\n            limit=round(bone_z1 - bone_z0, 2),\n            unit=\"mm\",\n            location=[0.0, 0.0, round(z0, 2)],\n            message=(\n                f\"plate footprint z={z0:.0f}..{z1:.0f} mm lies on the shaft \"\n                f\"(bone spans {bone_z0:.0f}..{bone_z1:.0f} mm)\"\n                if inside\n                else f\"plate footprint z={z0:.0f}..{z1:.0f} mm runs off the bone, which \"\n                     f\"spans {bone_z0:.0f}..{bone_z1:.0f} mm in the repo frame\"\n            ),\n        )\n    )\n\n    # 4. Screws lie within the footprint they are supposed to fix through.\n    zs = entries[:, 2]\n    outside = [\n        s[\"id\"] for s, z in zip(plan[\"screws\"], zs) if not (z0 - 1e-6 <= z <= z1 + 1e-6)\n    ]\n    checks.append(\n        Check(\n            id=\"plan_screws_within_footprint\",\n            status=PASS if not outside else FAIL,\n            value=float(len(outside)),\n            limit=0.0,\n            unit=\"count\",\n            message=(\n                \"every screw falls inside the plate footprint\"\n                if not outside\n                else f\"screw(s) {', '.join(outside)} lie outside footprint_z_mm \"\n                     f\"[{z0:.0f}, {z1:.0f}] -- the plate cannot reach them\"\n            ),\n        )\n    )\n\n    return Report.from_checks(\n        checks, meta={\"validator\": \"surgical_plan\", \"case_id\": plan.get(\"case_id\")}\n    )\n"}
{"Write":"C:\\TU\\Projects\\Agentic-Hackathon-Munich-EHL-Team-Harissa-\\autoimplants\\import_case.py: \"\"\"Turn a real CT-derived bone mesh plus a surgical plan into a runnable case.\n\n    python -m autoimplants.import_case \\\\\n        --case real_cases/<case_id>/surgical_plan.json \\\\\n        --bone real_cases/<case_id>/bone.stl\n\nThe importer is the whole boundary between \"clinical data as it actually\narrives\" and \"the locked input files this repo designs against\". It:\n\n  1. runs the mesh quality gate (autoimplants.mesh_quality)\n  2. computes the rigid transform into the repo frame from the plan's landmarks\n     (autoimplants.surgical_plan) and applies it to mesh, screws and keepouts\n  3. checks the transformed plan against the actual bone -- entries on the\n     surface, trajectories through bone, footprint on the shaft\n  4. writes bone.stl / case.json / screw_positions.json / keepout_zones.json in\n     exactly the shape the existing loop already reads\n\nNothing is invented. If the plan does not say where the screws go, the import\nfails; it does not pick positions. The synthetic demo in ``inputs/`` is\nuntouched and remains the default quick-start path.\n\nOutput goes to ``real_cases/<case_id>/generated/`` rather than ``inputs/``,\nbecause ``harness/guard.py`` locks ``inputs/*`` as system-controlled: a case\nimported into that directory would show up as a guard violation on the agent's\nown diff. Run an imported case by pointing --case at the generated case.json.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom . import mesh_quality, surgical_plan\nfrom .contracts import Report\nfrom .surgical_plan import PlanError\n\nREPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\n\n# Defaults for envelope fields a plan does not state. Ranges are the same\n# published bone-plate figures the synthetic case was built from; a plan that\n# cares should say so explicitly.\nDEFAULT_MAX_WIDTH_MM = 20.0\nDEFAULT_MAX_STANDOFF_MM = 6.0\nDEFAULT_THICKNESS_BOUNDS_MM = {\"min\": 2.5, \"max\": 4.5}\n\nPROVENANCE = (\n    \"REAL CT-DERIVED -- bone geometry segmented from patient imaging; surgical \"\n    \"planning supplied externally and treated as a locked, pre-solved input. \"\n    \"Imported by autoimplants.import_case. Verify the source data was \"\n    \"de-identified before it entered this repo. Research/demo tooling only: no \"\n    \"clinical, FDA, ISO or ASTM claim.\"\n)\n\n\ndef _write_json(path: Path, payload: dict) -> Path:\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + \"\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return path\n\n\ndef build_case_json(plan: dict, out_dir: Path) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The case.json the loop reads, assembled from the plan.\n\n    Paths are written relative to the case file so the generated directory is\n    self-contained and can be moved or archived whole.\n    \"\"\"\n    z0, z1 = (float(v) for v in plan[\"footprint_z_mm\"])\n    envelope = dict(plan.get(\"envelope\") or {})\n    envelope.setdefault(\"footprint_z_mm\", [z0, z1])\n    envelope.setdefault(\"aspect\", f\"{plan['approach']} {plan['bone']} shaft\")\n    envelope.setdefault(\"max_length_mm\", round(z1 - z0, 3))\n    envelope.setdefault(\"max_width_mm\", DEFAULT_MAX_WIDTH_MM)\n    envelope.setdefault(\"max_standoff_mm\", DEFAULT_MAX_STANDOFF_MM)\n    envelope.setdefault(\"thickness_bounds_mm\", dict(DEFAULT_THICKNESS_BOUNDS_MM))\n\n    thresholds = dict(plan[\"thresholds\"])\n    thresholds.setdefault(\"require_all_screws\", len(plan[\"screws\"]))\n\n    case = {\n        \"case_id\": plan[\"case_id\"],\n        \"provenance\": PROVENANCE,\n        \"source\": {\n            \"surgical_plan\": plan.get(\"_plan_path\"),\n            \"bone\": plan[\"bone\"],\n            \"side\": plan[\"side\"],\n            \"approach\": plan[\"approach\"],\n        },\n        \"inputs\": {\n            \"bone_mesh\": \"bone.stl\",\n            \"screw_positions\": \"screw_positions.json\",\n            \"keepout_zones\": \"keepout_zones.json\",\n        },\n        \"material\": dict(plan[\"material\"]),\n        \"envelope\": envelope,\n        \"thresholds\": thresholds,\n    }\n\n    if plan.get(\"load_cases\"):\n        case[\"load_cases\"] = plan[\"load_cases\"]\n    if plan.get(\"load_notes\"):\n        case[\"load_notes\"] = plan[\"load_notes\"]\n    if plan.get(\"iteration_budget\"):\n        case[\"iteration_budget\"] = plan[\"iteration_budget\"]\n\n    case[\"threshold_notes\"] = {\n        \"unenforced\": \"max_stress_MPa and min_screw_pullout_N are read only to \"\n                      \"populate limits -- every stress check returns SKIP until \"\n                      \"validators/stress.py is real.\",\n        \"frame\": \"All coordinates are in the repo frame (+Z along the shaft from \"\n                 \"the proximal landmark, +X the mount aspect). The rigid transform \"\n                 \"from the plan's original frame is recorded in frame_transform.json.\",\n    }\n    return case\n\n\ndef build_screw_positions(plan: dict) -> dict:\n    return {\n        \"provenance\": PROVENANCE,\n        \"note\": \"Surgical planning is a declared PRE-SOLVED input for this project. \"\n                \"These positions are locked: the implant must accommodate them, not \"\n                \"move them. Coordinates are in the repo frame.\",\n        \"bone_mesh\": \"bone.stl\",\n        \"screws\": [\n            {\n                \"id\": s[\"id\"],\n                \"index\": i,\n                \"entry_mm\": [round(float(c), 4) for c in s[\"entry_mm\"]],\n                \"direction\": [round(float(c), 6) for c in s[\"direction\"]],\n                \"diameter_mm\": float(s[\"diameter_mm\"]),\n                \"length_mm\": float(s[\"length_mm\"]),\n            }\n            for i, s in enumerate(plan[\"screws\"])\n        ],\n    }\n\n\ndef build_keepout_zones(plan: dict) -> dict:\n    return {\n        \"provenance\": PROVENANCE,\n        \"zones\": [\n            {\n                \"id\": z[\"id\"],\n                \"type\": \"sphere\",\n                \"center_mm\": [round(float(c), 4) for c in z[\"center_mm\"]],\n                \"radius_mm\": float(z[\"radius_mm\"]),\n                \"rationale\": z.get(\"rationale\", \"\"),\n            }\n            for z in plan[\"keepouts\"]\n        ],\n    }\n\n\ndef import_case(\n    plan_path: str | Path,\n    bone_path: str | Path,\n    out_dir: str | Path | None = None,\n    units: str = \"mm\",\n    max_faces: int = mesh_quality.MAX_FACES,\n) -> tuple[Report, Path | None]:\n    \"\"\"Run the full import. Returns the merged report and the case.json path.\n\n    The report is a normal ``Report``, so a failed import reads exactly like a\n    failed validation -- same table, same check ids, same JSON.\n    \"\"\"\n    plan = surgical_plan.load_plan(plan_path)\n\n    gate = mesh_quality.gate(bone_path, bone=plan[\"bone\"], units=units, max_faces=max_faces)\n    if not gate.passed:\n        return gate.report, None\n\n    transform = surgical_plan.frame_transform(plan)\n    mesh = gate.mesh.copy()\n    mesh.apply_transform(transform)\n\n    placed = surgical_plan.transformed_plan(plan, transform)\n    plan_report = surgical_plan.validate_against_bone(placed, mesh)\n\n    merged = Report.merge([gate.report, plan_report])\n    merged.meta[\"case_id\"] = plan[\"case_id\"]\n    if not merged.passed:\n        return merged, None\n\n    out = Path(out_dir) if out_dir else REPO_ROOT / \"real_cases\" / plan[\"case_id\"] / \"generated\"\n    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n    mesh.export(str(out / \"bone.stl\"))\n    case_path = _write_json(out / \"case.json\", build_case_json(placed, out))\n    _write_json(out / \"screw_positions.json\", build_screw_positions(placed))\n    _write_json(out / \"keepout_zones.json\", build_keepout_zones(placed))\n    _write_json(\n        out / \"frame_transform.json\",\n        {\n            \"note\": \"Rigid transform applied to the source mesh, screws and keepouts \"\n                    \"to bring them into the repo frame. Row-major 4x4, mm.\",\n            \"source_mesh\": str(Path(bone_path).resolve()),\n            \"source_plan\": plan.get(\"_plan_path\"),\n            \"matrix\": [[round(float(v), 9) for v in row] for row in transform],\n        },\n    )\n    merged.write(out / \"import_report.json\")\n\n    return merged, case_path\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"autoimplants.import_case\", description=__doc__)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--case\", required=True, help=\"surgical_plan.json for the real case\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--bone\", required=True, help=\"segmented bone mesh (STL/PLY/OBJ)\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--out\", help=\"output directory (default real_cases/<case_id>/generated)\")\n    ap.add_argument(\n        \"--units\",\n        default=\"mm\",\n        choices=sorted(mesh_quality.UNIT_SCALE_MM),\n        help=\"units the bone mesh is written in (default mm)\",\n    )\n    ap.add_argument(\"--max-faces\", type=int, default=mesh_quality.MAX_FACES)\n    args = ap.parse_args(argv)\n\n    try:\n        report, case_path = import_case(\n            args.case, args.bone, args.out, units=args.units, max_faces=args.max_faces\n        )\n    except PlanError as exc:\n        # A rejected plan is the expected outcome for incomplete planning data,\n        # not a crash. Print it the way every other failure in this repo prints.\n        print(f\"surgical plan rejected: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n\n    print(report.summary())\n\n    if case_path is None:\n        print(\"\\nimport failed -- no case was written\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n\n    if any(part == \"inputs\" for part in case_path.resolve().parts):\n        print(\n            \"\\n[warn] this case was written inside inputs/, which harness/guard.py \"\n            \"locks as system-controlled. Committing it will read as a guard violation.\",\n            file=sys.stderr,\n        )\n\n    rel = case_path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT) if case_path.is_relative_to(REPO_ROOT) else case_path\n    print(f\"\\nimported case written to {rel.parent}\")\n    print(\"run it with:\")\n    print(f\"  python -m autoimplants.run --case {rel.as_posix()} --validators geometry,stress\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"}

{"Write":"C:\\TU\\Projects\\Agentic-Hackathon-Munich-EHL-Team-Harissa-\\real_cases\\example\\make_example.py: \"\"\"Generate the worked example of a real-style case, in an arbitrary scanner frame.\n\nReal CT data cannot be committed to this repo -- it is large, and it is patient\ndata. So the example that exercises the import path is built from the synthetic\nfemur instead, deliberately rotated and translated out of the repo frame into a\nplausible scanner frame.\n\nThat is the point: the mesh and the plan arrive nowhere near axis-aligned, the\nway a real segmentation does, and ``autoimplants.import_case`` has to recover the\nframe from the landmarks. Because the ground truth is known exactly -- it is\n``inputs/`` before the transform -- the round trip is testable, which is what\n``tests/test_import_case.py`` checks.\n\nRun:  python real_cases/example/make_example.py\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport trimesh\n\nHERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nREPO_ROOT = HERE.parent.parent\nINPUTS = REPO_ROOT / \"inputs\"\n\nCASE_ID = \"EXAMPLE-FEMUR-CT-001\"\n\n# An arbitrary rigid pose standing in for scanner coordinates: obliquely angled,\n# origin far from the bone. Fixed numbers so the example is regenerable and\n# diffable, like inputs/make_bone.py.\nROT_DEG = (19.0, -34.0, 71.0)\nTRANSLATION_MM = (-118.5, 342.0, -87.25)\n\n# Shaft centreline of the synthetic femur is (bow(s), 0, z); see inputs/make_bone.py.\n# These are the landmarks a surgeon or planning tool would place, expressed in the\n# repo frame before the pose is applied.\nLANDMARK_PROXIMAL_REPO = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]\nLANDMARK_DISTAL_REPO = [0.0, 0.0, 400.0]\nLANDMARK_MOUNT_REPO = [35.0, 0.0, 200.0]  # on the +X aspect at mid-shaft\n\nPROVENANCE = (\n    \"SYNTHETIC STAND-IN FOR REAL DATA -- the synthetic femur from inputs/, rigidly \"\n    \"transformed into an arbitrary scanner-like frame so the import path can be \"\n    \"exercised and tested without committing patient imaging. Not patient data. \"\n    \"No clinical or regulatory claim.\"\n)\n\n\ndef scanner_pose() -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"The fixed 4x4 pose this example is written in.\"\"\"\n    rx, ry, rz = np.radians(ROT_DEG)\n    pose = trimesh.transformations.euler_matrix(rx, ry, rz, \"sxyz\")\n    pose[:3, 3] = TRANSLATION_MM\n    return pose\n\n\ndef _apply_points(points, pose):\n    pts = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(points, dtype=float))\n    return pts @ pose[:3, :3].T + pose[:3, 3]\n\n\ndef _apply_dirs(dirs, pose):\n    return np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(dirs, dtype=float)) @ pose[:3, :3].T\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    pose = scanner_pose()\n\n    mesh = trimesh.load(str(INPUTS / \"bone.stl\"), force=\"mesh\")\n    mesh.apply_transform(pose)\n    mesh.export(str(HERE / \"bone.stl\"))\n\n    case = json.loads((INPUTS / \"case.json\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    screws = json.loads((INPUTS / \"screw_positions.json\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))[\"screws\"]\n    zones = json.loads((INPUTS / \"keepout_zones.json\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))[\"zones\"]\n\n    plan = {\n        \"case_id\": CASE_ID,\n        \"provenance\": PROVENANCE,\n        \"bone\": \"femur\",\n        \"side\": \"right\",\n        \"approach\": \"lateral\",\n        \"coordinate_frame\": {\n            \"note\": \"Landmarks are in the same frame as bone.stl. The importer \"\n                    \"derives the repo frame from them: +Z proximal to distal, \"\n                    \"origin at the proximal landmark, +X the mount aspect.\",\n            \"landmarks\": {\n                \"proximal_shaft_mm\": _apply_points(LANDMARK_PROXIMAL_REPO, pose)[0].tolist(),\n                \"distal_shaft_mm\": _apply_points(LANDMARK_DISTAL_REPO, pose)[0].tolist(),\n                \"mount_side_mm\": _apply_points(LANDMARK_MOUNT_REPO, pose)[0].tolist(),\n            },\n        },\n        \"footprint_z_mm\": case[\"envelope\"][\"footprint_z_mm\"],\n        \"screws\": [\n            {\n                \"id\": s[\"id\"],\n                \"entry_mm\": _apply_points(s[\"entry_mm\"], pose)[0].tolist(),\n                \"direction\": _apply_dirs(s[\"direction\"], pose)[0].tolist(),\n                \"diameter_mm\": s[\"diameter_mm\"],\n                \"length_mm\": s[\"length_mm\"],\n            }\n            for s in screws\n        ],\n        \"keepouts\": [\n            {\n                \"id\": z[\"id\"],\n                \"type\": \"sphere\",\n                \"center_mm\": _apply_points(z[\"center_mm\"], pose)[0].tolist(),\n                \"radius_mm\": z[\"radius_mm\"],\n                \"rationale\": z.get(\"rationale\", \"\"),\n            }\n            for z in zones\n        ],\n        \"material\": case[\"material\"],\n        \"envelope\": {\n            \"max_width_mm\": case[\"envelope\"][\"max_width_mm\"],\n            \"max_standoff_mm\": case[\"envelope\"][\"max_standoff_mm\"],\n            \"thickness_bounds_mm\": case[\"envelope\"][\"thickness_bounds_mm\"],\n        },\n        \"thresholds\": case[\"thresholds\"],\n        \"load_cases\": case[\"load_cases\"],\n        \"load_notes\": \"Copied from the synthetic case. A real case would carry the \"\n                      \"patient's own load estimate.\",\n        \"iteration_budget\": case[\"iteration_budget\"],\n    }\n\n    (HERE / \"surgical_plan.json\").write_text(\n        json.dumps(plan, indent=2) + \"\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\"\n    )\n\n    print(f\"wrote {HERE / 'bone.stl'} ({len(mesh.faces)} faces)\")\n    print(f\"wrote {HERE / 'surgical_plan.json'} ({len(plan['screws'])} screws)\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"}

{"Edit":{"file_path":"C:\\TU\\Projects\\Agentic-Hackathon-Munich-EHL-Team-Harissa-\\autoimplants\\mesh_quality.py","adds":"def longest_extent_mm(mesh) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Longest distance across the mesh, independent of its orientation.\n\n    Not the bounding box: a mesh arrives in scanner coordinates, obliquely\n    angled, and the axis-aligned extents of a 400 mm femur lying at 30 degrees\n    are all well under 400 mm. Measuring the box would report a real femur as\n    implausibly short. The convex hull gives the true span.\n    \"\"\"\n    hull = mesh.convex_hull.vertices\n    if len(hull) > 2000:  # keep the pairwise distance matrix bounded\n        idx = np.linspace(0, len(hull) - 1, 2000).astype(int)\n        hull = hull[idx]\n    diffs = hull[:, None, :] - hull[None, :, :]\n    return float(np.sqrt((diffs ** 2).sum(axis=-1)).max())\n\n\ndef _check_units(mesh, bone: str, unit_scale: float) -> Check:\n    extent = longest_extent_mm(mesh)","removes":"def _check_units(mesh, bone: str, unit_scale: float) -> Check:\n    extent = float(np.max(mesh.bounds[1] - mesh.bounds[0]))","removesTruncated":false}}

{"Write":"C:\\TU\\Projects\\Agentic-Hackathon-Munich-EHL-Team-Harissa-\\tests\\test_surgical_plan.py: \"\"\"A plan this repo cannot design against must be rejected, by name.\n\nThe failure mode these tests exist to prevent is the quiet one: an incomplete\nplan that imports anyway, because some default filled the hole, and produces an\nimplant fitted to numbers nobody supplied.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pytest\n\nfrom autoimplants import surgical_plan\nfrom autoimplants.surgical_plan import PlanError\n\n\ndef test_example_plan_is_structurally_valid(example_plan):\n    surgical_plan.validate_structure(example_plan)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"field\", surgical_plan.REQUIRED_FIELDS)\ndef test_missing_required_field_is_rejected_by_name(example_plan, field):\n    plan = dict(example_plan)\n    plan.pop(field)\n    with pytest.raises(PlanError) as exc:\n        surgical_plan.validate_structure(plan)\n    assert field in str(exc.value)\n\n\ndef test_missing_landmarks_are_rejected(example_plan):\n    plan = dict(example_plan)\n    plan[\"coordinate_frame\"] = {\"note\": \"no landmarks, no axes\"}\n    with pytest.raises(PlanError) as exc:\n        surgical_plan.validate_structure(plan)\n    assert \"landmarks\" in str(exc.value)\n\n\ndef test_partial_landmarks_are_rejected(example_plan):\n    plan = json.loads(json.dumps(example_plan))\n    plan[\"coordinate_frame\"][\"landmarks\"].pop(\"mount_side_mm\")\n    with pytest.raises(PlanError) as exc:\n        surgical_plan.validate_structure(plan)\n    assert \"mount_side_mm\" in str(exc.value)\n\n\ndef test_zero_length_screw_direction_is_rejected(example_plan):\n    plan = json.loads(json.dumps(example_plan))\n    plan[\"screws\"][2][\"direction\"] = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]\n    with pytest.raises(PlanError) as exc:\n        surgical_plan.validate_structure(plan)\n    assert \"screws[2]\" in str(exc.value)\n\n\ndef test_unnormalised_screw_direction_is_accepted_and_normalised(example_plan):\n    \"\"\"Magnitude carries no meaning; only the zero vector is an error.\"\"\"\n    plan = json.loads(json.dumps(example_plan))\n    plan[\"screws\"][0][\"direction\"] = [\n        7.0 * c for c in plan[\"screws\"][0][\"direction\"]\n    ]\n    surgical_plan.validate_structure(plan)\n\n    transform = surgical_plan.frame_transform(plan)\n    placed = surgical_plan.transformed_plan(plan, transform)\n    assert np.isclose(np.linalg.norm(placed[\"screws\"][0][\"direction\"]), 1.0)\n\n\ndef test_no_screws_is_rejected(example_plan):\n    plan = dict(example_plan)\n    plan[\"screws\"] = []\n    with pytest.raises(PlanError):\n        surgical_plan.validate_structure(plan)\n\n\ndef test_malformed_keepout_is_rejected(example_plan):\n    plan = json.loads(json.dumps(example_plan))\n    plan[\"keepouts\"][0][\"radius_mm\"] = -3.0\n    with pytest.raises(PlanError) as exc:\n        surgical_plan.validate_structure(plan)\n    assert \"radius_mm\" in str(exc.value)\n\n\ndef test_non_sphere_keepout_is_rejected(example_plan):\n    plan = json.loads(json.dumps(example_plan))\n    plan[\"keepouts\"][0][\"type\"] = \"cylinder\"\n    with pytest.raises(PlanError) as exc:\n        surgical_plan.validate_structure(plan)\n    assert \"sphere\" in str(exc.value)\n\n\ndef test_backwards_footprint_is_rejected(example_plan):\n    plan = dict(example_plan)\n    plan[\"footprint_z_mm\"] = [280.0, 100.0]\n    with pytest.raises(PlanError):\n        surgical_plan.validate_structure(plan)\n\n\n# -- the frame transform -------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_frame_transform_inverts_the_known_pose(example_plan):\n    \"\"\"The example is the synthetic femur under a known pose, so the recovered\n    transform must be that pose's inverse -- to floating point.\"\"\"\n    import sys\n    sys.path.insert(0, str(surgical_plan.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\n                           / \"real_cases\" / \"example\"))\n    from make_example import scanner_pose  # noqa: PLC0415\n\n    recovered = surgical_plan.frame_transform(example_plan)\n    assert np.allclose(recovered @ scanner_pose(), np.eye(4), atol=1e-6)\n\n\ndef test_frame_transform_is_rigid(example_plan):\n    t = surgical_plan.frame_transform(example_plan)\n    rotation = t[:3, :3]\n    assert np.allclose(rotation @ rotation.T, np.eye(3), atol=1e-9)\n    assert np.isclose(np.linalg.det(rotation), 1.0, atol=1e-9)\n\n\ndef test_mount_landmark_on_the_axis_is_ambiguous(example_plan):\n    \"\"\"A mount-side landmark on the shaft axis does not say which way is out.\"\"\"\n    plan = json.loads(json.dumps(example_plan))\n    lm = plan[\"coordinate_frame\"][\"landmarks\"]\n    proximal = np.array(lm[\"proximal_shaft_mm\"])\n    distal = np.array(lm[\"distal_shaft_mm\"])\n    lm[\"mount_side_mm\"] = (proximal + 0.5 * (distal - proximal)).tolist()\n\n    with pytest.raises(PlanError) as exc:\n        surgical_plan.frame_transform(plan)\n    assert \"ambiguous\" in str(exc.value)\n\n\ndef test_collapsed_shaft_landmarks_are_rejected(example_plan):\n    plan = json.loads(json.dumps(example_plan))\n    lm = plan[\"coordinate_frame\"][\"landmarks\"]\n    lm[\"distal_shaft_mm\"] = (np.array(lm[\"proximal_shaft_mm\"]) + 3.0).tolist()\n\n    with pytest.raises(PlanError) as exc:\n        surgical_plan.frame_transform(plan)\n    assert \"shaft axis\" in str(exc.value)\n\n\ndef test_explicit_axes_are_honoured():\n    \"\"\"A plan may state the frame outright instead of via landmarks.\"\"\"\n    plan = {\n        \"coordinate_frame\": {\n            \"axes\": {\n                \"shaft\": [0.0, 0.0, 2.0],\n                \"mount_side\": [9.0, 0.0, 0.0],\n                \"origin_mm\": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0],\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    t = surgical_plan.frame_transform(plan)\n    moved = surgical_plan.transform_points([[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]], t)[0]\n    assert np.allclose(moved, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], atol=1e-9)\n\n\ndef test_transformed_plan_preserves_relative_geometry(example_plan):\n    \"\"\"A change of frame must not move anything relative to anything else.\"\"\"\n    t = surgical_plan.frame_transform(example_plan)\n    placed = surgical_plan.transformed_plan(example_plan, t)\n\n    before = np.array([s[\"entry_mm\"] for s in example_plan[\"screws\"]])\n    after = np.array([s[\"entry_mm\"] for s in placed[\"screws\"]])\n    d_before = np.linalg.norm(before[0] - before[-1])\n    d_after = np.linalg.norm(after[0] - after[-1])\n    assert np.isclose(d_before, d_after, atol=1e-6)\n"}
{"Write":"C:\\TU\\Projects\\Agentic-Hackathon-Munich-EHL-Team-Harissa-\\tests\\test_mesh_quality.py: \"\"\"The mesh gate has to reject exactly the meshes a real segmentation produces.\n\nEach test builds the defect deliberately, because none of them can be produced by\ninputs/make_bone.py -- that is the point of the gate.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pytest\nimport trimesh\n\nfrom autoimplants import mesh_quality\n\nREPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nBONE = REPO_ROOT / \"inputs\" / \"bone.stl\"\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef bone() -> trimesh.Trimesh:\n    return trimesh.load(str(BONE), force=\"mesh\")\n\n\ndef _write(mesh, tmp_path, name=\"mesh.stl\") -> str:\n    path = tmp_path / name\n    mesh.export(str(path))\n    return str(path)\n\n\ndef test_clean_bone_passes(tmp_path, bone):\n    result = mesh_quality.gate(_write(bone, tmp_path), bone=\"femur\")\n    assert result.passed\n    assert result.mesh is not None\n\n\ndef test_missing_file_errors_without_raising(tmp_path):\n    result = mesh_quality.gate(tmp_path / \"nope.stl\", bone=\"femur\")\n    assert not result.passed\n    assert result.mesh is None\n\n\ndef test_metre_scale_mesh_is_rejected_with_a_hint(tmp_path, bone):\n    \"\"\"A femur written in metres passes every mm threshold meaninglessly.\"\"\"\n    tiny = bone.copy()\n    tiny.apply_scale(0.001)\n    result = mesh_quality.gate(_write(tiny, tmp_path), bone=\"femur\")\n\n    assert not result.passed\n    check = result.report.by_id(\"mesh_units_plausible\")\n    assert check.status == \"FAIL\"\n    assert \"--units m\" in check.message\n\n\ndef test_declared_units_are_applied(tmp_path, bone):\n    \"\"\"The same file passes once the caller says what units it is in.\"\"\"\n    in_cm = bone.copy()\n    in_cm.apply_scale(0.1)\n    result = mesh_quality.gate(_write(in_cm, tmp_path), bone=\"femur\", units=\"cm\")\n\n    assert result.passed\n    assert any(\"scaled from cm\" in r for r in result.repairs)\n\n\ndef test_longest_extent_ignores_orientation(bone):\n    \"\"\"A rotated femur is still 400 mm long, whatever its bounding box says.\"\"\"\n    straight = mesh_quality.longest_extent_mm(bone)\n\n    tilted = bone.copy()\n    tilted.apply_transform(trimesh.transformations.euler_matrix(0.4, -0.7, 1.1))\n    assert np.isclose(straight, mesh_quality.longest_extent_mm(tilted), rtol=1e-6)\n\n    # The bounding box, which this replaced, does not survive the rotation.\n    assert float(np.max(tilted.bounds[1] - tilted.bounds[0])) < straight - 10.0\n\n\ndef test_speckle_islands_are_dropped(tmp_path, bone):\n    \"\"\"Segmentation noise is removed, not treated as anatomy.\"\"\"\n    speck = trimesh.creation.icosphere(radius=1.5)\n    speck.apply_translation([90.0, 90.0, 90.0])\n    dirty = trimesh.util.concatenate([bone, speck])\n\n    result = mesh_quality.gate(_write(dirty, tmp_path), bone=\"femur\")\n\n    assert result.passed\n    assert any(\"speckle island\" in r for r in result.repairs)\n    # The island is gone, so the mesh bounds no longer reach out to it.\n    assert result.mesh.bounds[1][0] < 80.0\n\n\ndef test_second_comparable_component_fails(tmp_path, bone):\n    \"\"\"Two bones in the field of view is a human decision, not an auto-repair.\"\"\"\n    second = bone.copy()\n    second.apply_translation([200.0, 0.0, 0.0])\n    both = trimesh.util.concatenate([bone, second])\n\n    result = mesh_quality.gate(_write(both, tmp_path), bone=\"femur\")\n\n    assert not result.passed\n    assert result.report.by_id(\"mesh_single_component\").status == \"FAIL\"\n\n\ndef test_open_mesh_is_repaired_or_reported(tmp_path, bone):\n    \"\"\"Containment queries are undefined on an open surface, so it cannot pass silently.\"\"\"\n    holed = bone.copy()\n    keep = np.ones(len(holed.faces), dtype=bool)\n    keep[:40] = False\n    holed.update_faces(keep)\n    assert not holed.is_watertight\n\n    result = mesh_quality.gate(_write(holed, tmp_path), bone=\"femur\")\n    check = result.report.by_id(\"mesh_watertight\")\n\n    if check.status == \"PASS\":\n        assert result.mesh.is_watertight\n        assert any(\"filled holes\" in r for r in result.repairs)\n    else:\n        assert result.mesh is None\n\n\ndef test_face_budget_reported(tmp_path, bone):\n    \"\"\"A mesh over budget is either decimated or explicitly flagged as slow.\"\"\"\n    result = mesh_quality.gate(_write(bone, tmp_path), bone=\"femur\", max_faces=500)\n    check = result.report.by_id(\"mesh_face_budget\")\n    assert check.status == \"PASS\"\n    assert check.value <= 500 or \"decimation is unavailable\" in check.message\n"}
{"Write":"C:\\TU\\Projects\\Agentic-Hackathon-Munich-EHL-Team-Harissa-\\tests\\test_import_case.py: \"\"\"End to end: an obliquely posed real-style case must import to the repo frame.\n\nThe example case is the synthetic femur under a known rigid pose, so the import\nhas an exact expected answer -- ``inputs/`` itself. Anything the frame recovery\ngets wrong shows up here as a millimetre-scale disagreement with the ground truth.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pytest\nimport trimesh\n\nfrom autoimplants import import_case\nfrom autoimplants.surgical_plan import PlanError\n\nREPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nINPUTS = REPO_ROOT / \"inputs\"\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef imported(tmp_path, example_plan_path, example_bone_path):\n    report, case_path = import_case.import_case(\n        example_plan_path, example_bone_path, out_dir=tmp_path / \"generated\"\n    )\n    assert report.passed, report.summary()\n    assert case_path is not None\n    return case_path\n\n\ndef test_import_writes_the_locked_input_shape(imported):\n    out = imported.parent\n    for name in (\"bone.stl\", \"case.json\", \"screw_positions.json\", \"keepout_zones.json\"):\n        assert (out / name).exists(), f\"{name} was not written\"\n\n\ndef test_screws_round_trip_to_the_synthetic_ground_truth(imported, synthetic_screws):\n    got = json.loads((imported.parent / \"screw_positions.json\").read_text(\"utf-8\"))[\"screws\"]\n    assert len(got) == len(synthetic_screws)\n\n    for a, b in zip(got, synthetic_screws):\n        assert a[\"id\"] == b[\"id\"]\n        assert np.allclose(a[\"entry_mm\"], b[\"entry_mm\"], atol=1e-3)\n        assert np.allclose(a[\"direction\"], b[\"direction\"], atol=1e-6)\n\n\ndef test_keepouts_round_trip_to_the_synthetic_ground_truth(imported):\n    got = json.loads((imported.parent / \"keepout_zones.json\").read_text(\"utf-8\"))[\"zones\"]\n    want = json.loads((INPUTS / \"keepout_zones.json\").read_text(\"utf-8\"))[\"zones\"]\n\n    for a, b in zip(got, want):\n        assert a[\"id\"] == b[\"id\"]\n        assert np.allclose(a[\"center_mm\"], b[\"center_mm\"], atol=1e-3)\n        assert a[\"radius_mm\"] == b[\"radius_mm\"]\n\n\ndef test_mesh_lands_back_in_the_repo_frame(imported):\n    got = trimesh.load(str(imported.parent / \"bone.stl\"), force=\"mesh\")\n    want = trimesh.load(str(INPUTS / \"bone.stl\"), force=\"mesh\")\n    assert np.allclose(got.bounds, want.bounds, atol=1e-2)\n\n\ndef test_case_json_points_at_its_own_files(imported):\n    case = json.loads(imported.read_text(\"utf-8\"))\n    assert case[\"inputs\"][\"bone_mesh\"] == \"bone.stl\"\n\n    from autoimplants import case_io\n\n    loaded = case_io.load_case(imported)\n    assert case_io.bone_path(loaded) == (imported.parent / \"bone.stl\").resolve()\n    assert len(case_io.load_screws(loaded)) == 6\n\n\ndef test_transform_is_recorded_for_traceability(imported):\n    recorded = json.loads((imported.parent / \"frame_transform.json\").read_text(\"utf-8\"))\n    matrix = np.array(recorded[\"matrix\"])\n    assert matrix.shape == (4, 4)\n    assert np.allclose(matrix[:3, :3] @ matrix[:3, :3].T, np.eye(3), atol=1e-9)\n\n\ndef test_plan_mesh_mismatch_is_caught(tmp_path, example_plan, example_bone_path):\n    \"\"\"A plan describing a different scan must not import silently.\"\"\"\n    plan = json.loads(json.dumps(example_plan))\n    for s in plan[\"screws\"]:\n        s[\"entry_mm\"] = [c + 25.0 for c in s[\"entry_mm\"]]\n\n    plan_path = tmp_path / \"surgical_plan.json\"\n    plan_path.write_text(json.dumps(plan), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n    report, case_path = import_case.import_case(\n        plan_path, example_bone_path, out_dir=tmp_path / \"generated\"\n    )\n    assert not report.passed\n    assert case_path is None\n    assert report.by_id(\"plan_screw_entries_on_bone\").status == \"FAIL\"\n\n\ndef test_footprint_off_the_bone_is_caught(tmp_path, example_plan, example_bone_path):\n    plan = json.loads(json.dumps(example_plan))\n    plan[\"footprint_z_mm\"] = [500.0, 700.0]\n\n    plan_path = tmp_path / \"surgical_plan.json\"\n    plan_path.write_text(json.dumps(plan), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n    report, case_path = import_case.import_case(\n        plan_path, example_bone_path, out_dir=tmp_path / \"generated\"\n    )\n    assert not report.passed\n    assert case_path is None\n    assert report.by_id(\"plan_footprint_within_bone\").status == \"FAIL\"\n\n\ndef test_incomplete_plan_raises_rather_than_guessing(tmp_path, example_plan, example_bone_path):\n    plan = dict(example_plan)\n    plan.pop(\"screws\")\n    plan_path = tmp_path / \"surgical_plan.json\"\n    plan_path.write_text(json.dumps(plan), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n    with pytest.raises(PlanError):\n        import_case.import_case(plan_path, example_bone_path, out_dir=tmp_path / \"generated\")\n\n\ndef test_imported_case_runs_the_existing_geometry_validator(imported):\n    \"\"\"The whole point: an imported case is just a case.\"\"\"\n    from autoimplants import case_io\n    from autoimplants.validators import run_one\n\n    case = case_io.set_active_case(case_io.load_case(imported), imported)\n    report = run_one(\"geometry\", str(REPO_ROOT / \"out\" / \"implant.stl\"), case)\n\n    if report.by_id(\"geometry_crashed\") or report.by_id(\"geometry_import\"):\n        pytest.skip(\"no exported implant to validate; run autoimplants.run first\")\n\n    assert report.by_id(\"bone_conformance_gap\") is not None\n    assert report.meta[\"bone_mesh\"].endswith(\"bone.stl\")\n"}
{"Write":"C:\\TU\\Projects\\Agentic-Hackathon-Munich-EHL-Team-Harissa-\\tests\\test_geometry_generalised.py: \"\"\"The two geometry assumptions that only held for the synthetic case.\n\nBoth were correct for ``inputs/`` and wrong for anything else: screws were assumed\nto run along -X, and the bone gap was read off the y=0 centreline. A real plan has\nobliquely angled screws, and a real shaft curves in both planes.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pytest\nimport trimesh\n\nfrom autoimplants import case_io\nfrom autoimplants.validators import geometry\n\nOBLIQUE = np.array([-0.80, 0.36, 0.48])\nOBLIQUE /= np.linalg.norm(OBLIQUE)\n\nHOLE_D_MM = 4.5\n\n\ndef _plate_with_bore(direction: np.ndarray, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"A plate with one clean bore along ``direction`` through its centre.\"\"\"\n    plate = trimesh.creation.box(extents=(6.0, 20.0, 60.0))\n    align = trimesh.geometry.align_vectors([0.0, 0.0, 1.0], direction)\n    bore = trimesh.creation.cylinder(radius=HOLE_D_MM / 2.0, height=200.0, transform=align)\n\n    drilled = trimesh.boolean.difference([plate, bore])\n    path = tmp_path / \"plate.stl\"\n    drilled.export(str(path))\n    return drilled\n\n\ndef _case_with_screw(direction, tmp_path, entry=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"A minimal case whose single screw runs along ``direction``.\"\"\"\n    screws = {\n        \"screws\": [\n            {\n                \"id\": \"screw_0\",\n                \"index\": 0,\n                \"entry_mm\": list(entry),\n                \"direction\": list(direction),\n                \"diameter_mm\": HOLE_D_MM,\n                \"length_mm\": 30.0,\n            }\n        ]\n    }\n    screws_path = tmp_path / \"screw_positions.json\"\n    screws_path.write_text(json.dumps(screws), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n    return {\n        \"case_id\": \"TEST\",\n        \"inputs\": {\"screw_positions\": str(screws_path), \"keepout_zones\": str(tmp_path / \"none.json\")},\n        \"thresholds\": {\"require_all_screws\": 1},\n    }\n\n\ndef test_oblique_bore_reads_as_clear(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"The bore is drilled along the screw's own axis, so the screw is unobstructed.\"\"\"\n    mesh = _plate_with_bore(OBLIQUE, tmp_path)\n    case = _case_with_screw(OBLIQUE, tmp_path)\n\n    check = geometry.check_screws(mesh, case)[0]\n    assert check.status == \"PASS\", check.message\n\n\ndef test_oblique_screw_through_solid_reads_as_blocked(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Same plate, a screw on a different oblique axis: it hits material.\"\"\"\n    mesh = _plate_with_bore(OBLIQUE, tmp_path)\n    other = np.array([-0.55, -0.70, 0.45])\n    other /= np.linalg.norm(other)\n    case = _case_with_screw(other, tmp_path)\n\n    check = geometry.check_screws(mesh, case)[0]\n    assert check.status == \"FAIL\"\n    assert \"screw_0\" in check.message\n\n\ndef test_axis_aligned_case_still_behaves(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Generalising the ring must not change the verdict it already gave.\"\"\"\n    axis = np.array([-1.0, 0.0, 0.0])\n    mesh = _plate_with_bore(axis, tmp_path)\n    case = _case_with_screw(axis, tmp_path)\n\n    assert geometry.check_screws(mesh, case)[0].status == {"Write":"C:\\TU\\Projects\\Agentic-Hackathon-Munich-EHL-Team-Harissa-\\autoimplants\\dicom_to_mesh.py: \"\"\"Phase 2: raw DICOM series to a candidate bone mesh.\n\n    python -m autoimplants.dicom_to_mesh \\\\\n        --dicom-dir <dir> --bone femur --out real_cases/<case_id>/bone.stl\n\nThis is deliberately a *separate* command from the implant loop. DICOM is\nscanner-slice data; it has to be segmented before anything in this repo can\ndesign against it, and segmentation is the step where clinical judgement lives.\nThreshold plus connected components is research/demo tooling -- it produces a\nplausible femur, not a correct one. Nobody should run the output straight into a\ndesign without looking at it, which is why the loop still consumes a mesh plus a\nsurgical plan and never a DICOM directory.\n\nWhat this does do honestly: read the series with its real spacing and\norientation, convert to Hounsfield units, threshold at a conservative cortical\nvalue, keep the largest connected component, and surface it with marching cubes\nin *patient* coordinates -- not index coordinates. Getting that transform wrong\nwould silently scale and shear the anatomy, and every millimetre threshold\ndownstream would be measuring a distorted bone.\n\nDependencies are not in requirements.txt: see requirements-dicom.txt. They are\nlarge, this is a phase-2 path, and the container that runs the design loop should\nnot pay for them.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom . import mesh_quality\n\n# Cortical bone runs roughly 300-1900 HU; trabecular bone overlaps soft tissue\n# below that. Starting conservatively (high) keeps soft tissue out at the cost of\n# thinning the cortex, which is the safer error for a surface nobody should trust\n# without review.\nDEFAULT_THRESHOLD_HU = 300.0\n\n# DICOM tags that carry direct identifiers. Not an exhaustive de-identification\n# audit -- enough to notice that a series was never de-identified at all.\nPHI_TAGS = {\n    \"PatientName\": (0x0010, 0x0010),\n    \"PatientID\": (0x0010, 0x0020),\n    \"PatientBirthDate\": (0x0010, 0x0030),\n    \"PatientAddress\": (0x0010, 0x1040),\n    \"PatientTelephoneNumbers\": (0x0010, 0x2154),\n    \"OtherPatientIDs\": (0x0010, 0x1000),\n    \"ReferringPhysicianName\": (0x0008, 0x0090),\n    \"InstitutionName\": (0x0008, 0x0080),\n    \"AccessionNumber\": (0x0008, 0x0050),\n    \"StudyDate\": (0x0008, 0x0020),\n}\n\n\nclass DicomError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A DICOM directory this tool cannot turn into a volume.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _require(module: str):\n    try:\n        return __import__(module)\n    except ImportError as exc:  # noqa: PERF203\n        raise DicomError(\n            f\"{module} is not installed. DICOM support is optional and lives in \"\n            f\"requirements-dicom.txt:\\n    uv pip install -r requirements-dicom.txt\"\n        ) from exc\n\n\n# -- reading ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef scan_for_phi(dicom_dir: str | Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Identifying tags that are populated in the first slice of the series.\n\n    Reported, never stripped: de-identification is the data owner's decision and\n    their audit trail, not something a mesh tool should do quietly on the way past.\n    \"\"\"\n    pydicom = _require(\"pydicom\")\n\n    files = sorted(Path(dicom_dir).rglob(\"*\"))\n    for f in files:\n        if not f.is_file():\n            continue\n        try:\n            ds = pydicom.dcmread(str(f), stop_before_pixels=True, force=True)\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n        found = {}\n        for name, tag in PHI_TAGS.items():\n            value = ds.get(tag)\n            if value is not None and str(value.value).strip():\n                found[name] = str(value.value)\n        return found\n    raise DicomError(f\"no readable DICOM files under {dicom_dir}\")\n\n\ndef load_series(dicom_dir: str | Path):\n    \"\"\"Read a DICOM series into an HU volume plus its index-to-patient affine.\n\n    Returns ``(volume, affine)`` where ``volume`` is indexed ``[z, y, x]`` in\n    Hounsfield units and ``affine`` is the 4x4 mapping a continuous ``(x, y, z)``\n    index to patient coordinates in mm.\n    \"\"\"\n    sitk = _require(\"SimpleITK\")\n\n    reader = sitk.ImageSeriesReader()\n    series = reader.GetGDCMSeriesIDs(str(dicom_dir))\n    if not series:\n        raise DicomError(f\"no DICOM series found under {dicom_dir}\")\n    if len(series) > 1:\n        # Picking one silently is how you segment the scout scan by accident.\n        raise DicomError(\n            f\"{len(series)} DICOM series found under {dicom_dir}. Point --dicom-dir \"\n            f\"at a single series: {', '.join(series)}\"\n        )\n\n    files = reader.GetGDCMSeriesFileNames(str(dicom_dir), series[0])\n    reader.SetFileNames(files)\n    image = reader.Execute()\n\n    volume = sitk.GetArrayFromImage(image).astype(np.float32)  # [z, y, x], HU\n\n    spacing = np.array(image.GetSpacing(), dtype=float)          # (x, y, z) mm\n    direction = np.array(image.GetDirection(), dtype=float).reshape(3, 3)\n    origin = np.array(image.GetOrigin(), dtype=float)\n\n    affine = np.eye(4)\n    affine[:3, :3] = direction @ np.diag(spacing)\n    affine[:3, 3] = origin\n    return volume, affine\n\n\n# -- segmentation -------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef segment_bone(volume: np.ndarray, threshold_hu: float = DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_HU) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Binary mask of the largest connected structure above ``threshold_hu``.\n\n    The largest component is the bone in a cropped limb series. In a whole-pelvis\n    series it may be the pelvis, or two femurs bridged by a partial volume. The\n    mesh gate catches the bridged case; the rest is why the output needs review.\n    \"\"\"\n    ndimage = _require(\"scipy\").ndimage\n\n    mask = volume >= float(threshold_hu)\n    if not mask.any():\n        raise DicomError(\n            f\"no voxel reaches {threshold_hu:.0f} HU. Either the series is not CT, \"\n            f\"or the rescale slope/intercept were not applied -- check the source data\"\n        )\n\n    labels, n = ndimage.label(mask)\n    if n > 1:\n        sizes = ndimage.sum(mask, labels, index=range(1, n + 1))\n        mask = labels == (int(np.argmax(sizes)) + 1)\n\n    # Close pinholes left by the threshold in thin cortex, so marching cubes does\n    # not produce a surface riddled with holes the gate then has to repair.\n    return ndimage.binary_closing(mask, iterations=2)\n\n\ndef mask_to_mesh(mask: np.ndarray, affine: np.ndarray):\n    \"\"\"Surface the mask with marching cubes, in patient coordinates.\"\"\"\n    measure = _require(\"skimage.measure\")\n    trimesh = _require(\"trimesh\")\n\n    verts_zyx, faces, _, _ = measure.marching_cubes(mask.astype(np.uint8), level=0.5)\n\n    # marching_cubes indexes the array as [z, y, x]; the affine is built for\n    # (x, y, z) index order, so the columns have to be swapped before transforming.\n    verts_xyz = verts_zyx[:, ::-1]\n    verts = verts_xyz @ affine[:3, :3].T + affine[:3, 3]\n\n    mesh = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=verts, faces=faces, process=True)\n    mesh.fix_normals()\n    return mesh\n\n\ndef dicom_to_mesh(\n    dicom_dir: str | Path,\n    out_path: str | Path,\n    bone: str = \"femur\",\n    threshold_hu: float = DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_HU,\n    max_faces: int = mesh_quality.MAX_FACES,\n):\n    \"\"\"Full conversion, then the same mesh gate a hand-segmented mesh must pass.\"\"\"\n    volume, affine = load_series(dicom_dir)\n    mask = segment_bone(volume, threshold_hu)\n    mesh = mask_to_mesh(mask, affine)\n\n    out_path = Path(out_path)\n    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    mesh.export(str(out_path))\n\n    # The gate runs on what was written, so its verdict describes the artefact\n    # the next step will actually read.\n    return mesh_quality.gate(out_path, bone=bone, units=\"mm\", max_faces=max_faces)\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"autoimplants.dicom_to_mesh\", description=__doc__)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--dicom-dir\", required=True, help=\"directory holding one DICOM series\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--bone\", default=\"femur\", choices=sorted(mesh_quality.BONE_EXTENT_MM))\n    ap.add_argument(\"--out\", required=True, help=\"STL to write\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--threshold-hu\", type=float, default=DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_HU)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--max-faces\", type=int, default=mesh_quality.MAX_FACES)\n    args = ap.parse_args(argv)\n\n    try:\n        phi = scan_for_phi(args.dicom_dir)\n        if phi:\n            print(\n                \"WARNING: this DICOM series still carries direct identifiers: \"\n                + \", \".join(sorted(phi))\n                + \"\\nDe-identify the source data before it goes any further. Do not \"\n                  \"commit DICOM to this repository.\",\n                file=sys.stderr,\n            )\n\n        result = dicom_to_mesh(\n            args.dicom_dir,\n            args.out,\n            bone=args.bone,\n            threshold_hu=args.threshold_hu,\n            max_faces=args.max_faces,\n        )\n    except DicomError as exc:\n        print(f\"DICOM conversion failed: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n\n    print(result.report.summary())\n    print(f\"\\nwrote {args.out}\")\n    print(\n        \"\\nThis is threshold segmentation, not clinical segmentation. Open the mesh \"\n        \"and check it is the bone you meant before importing a case against it.\"\n    )\n    return 0 if result.passed else 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"}

{"Write":"C:\\TU\\Projects\\Agentic-Hackathon-Munich-EHL-Team-Harissa-\\tests\\test_dicom_to_mesh.py: \"\"\"DICOM conversion, exercised on a synthetic volume rather than patient imaging.\n\nA real dataset is too large to commit and is patient data besides, so the fixture\nis a shaft-shaped HU volume written to disk as an actual DICOM series. That is\nenough to catch the failure this path is most likely to have: getting the\nindex-to-patient transform wrong, which silently scales and shears the anatomy so\nthat every millimetre threshold downstream measures a distorted bone.\n\nEverything here skips cleanly when the optional dependencies are absent\n(requirements-dicom.txt), because the design loop does not need them.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pytest\n\nfrom autoimplants import dicom_to_mesh\nfrom autoimplants.dicom_to_mesh import DicomError\n\npytest.importorskip(\"scipy\", reason=\"requirements-dicom.txt not installed\")\npytest.importorskip(\"skimage\", reason=\"requirements-dicom.txt not installed\")\n\n# The synthetic scan: a 24 mm diameter shaft, 120 mm long, in a soft-tissue field.\nSPACING_XYZ = (0.8, 0.8, 1.25)   # anisotropic on purpose -- isotropic hides bugs\nSHAFT_RADIUS_MM = 12.0\nSHAFT_LENGTH_MM = 120.0\nBONE_HU = 900.0\nSOFT_TISSUE_HU = 40.0\n\n\ndef _synthetic_volume():\n    \"\"\"An HU volume plus the affine that maps its indices to patient mm.\"\"\"\n    nx = int(80 / SPACING_XYZ[0])\n    ny = int(80 / SPACING_XYZ[1])\n    nz = int(SHAFT_LENGTH_MM / SPACING_XYZ[2])\n\n    ix, iy = np.meshgrid(np.arange(nx), np.arange(ny), indexing=\"ij\")\n    cx, cy = nx / 2.0, ny / 2.0\n    r_mm = np.sqrt(\n        ((ix - cx) * SPACING_XYZ[0]) ** 2 + ((iy - cy) * SPACING_XYZ[1]) ** 2\n    )\n    slice_hu = np.where(r_mm <= SHAFT_RADIUS_MM, BONE_HU, SOFT_TISSUE_HU)\n\n    volume = np.repeat(slice_hu.T[None, :, :], nz, axis=0).astype(np.float32)\n\n    affine = np.eye(4)\n    affine[:3, :3] = np.diag(SPACING_XYZ)\n    affine[:3, 3] = [-100.0, 250.0, -60.0]  # an origin nowhere near the bone\n    return volume, affine\n\n\ndef test_threshold_keeps_bone_and_drops_soft_tissue():\n    volume, _ = _synthetic_volume()\n    mask = dicom_to_mesh.segment_bone(volume, threshold_hu=300.0)\n\n    assert mask.any()\n    assert not mask.all()\n    # Soft tissue is 40 HU: nothing outside the shaft should survive a 300 HU cut.\n    assert mask.sum() < volume.size * 0.5\n\n\ndef test_empty_threshold_is_an_error_not_an_empty_mesh():\n    volume = np.full((10, 10, 10), SOFT_TISSUE_HU, dtype=np.float32)\n    with pytest.raises(DicomError, match=\"HU\"):\n        dicom_to_mesh.segment_bone(volume, threshold_hu=300.0)\n\n\ndef test_mesh_lands_in_patient_coordinates_at_the_right_scale():\n    \"\"\"The whole point of carrying the affine: real mm, at the real origin.\"\"\"\n    volume, affine = _synthetic_volume()\n    mask = dicom_to_mesh.segment_bone(volume, threshold_hu=300.0)\n    mesh = dicom_to_mesh.mask_to_mesh(mask, affine)\n\n    extents = mesh.bounds[1] - mesh.bounds[0]\n\n    # Diameter across both transverse axes, length along the slice axis. The\n    # closing operation dilates by a voxel or so, hence the tolerance.\n    assert 2 * SHAFT_RADIUS_MM - 3 <= extents[0] <= 2 * SHAFT_RADIUS_MM + 4\n    assert 2 * SHAFT_RADIUS_MM - 3 <= extents[1] <= 2 * SHAFT_RADIUS_MM + 4\n    assert extents[2] >= SHAFT_LENGTH_MM - 5\n\n    # And it is positioned by the affine, not left at the array origin.\n    assert mesh.bounds[0][1] > 200.0\n\n\ndef test_anisotropic_spacing_is_not_confused_between_axes():\n    \"\"\"A z/x spacing mix-up would stretch the shaft: catch it by construction.\"\"\"\n    volume, affine = _synthetic_volume()\n    mask = dicom_to_mesh.segment_bone(volume, threshold_hu=300.0)\n    mesh = dicom_to_mesh.mask_to_mesh(mask, affine)\n\n    extents = mesh.bounds[1] - mesh.bounds[0]\n    assert np.isclose(extents[0], extents[1], atol=1.0), (\n        \"the two transverse axes have equal physical size; if they differ, the \"\n        \"spacing vector is being applied to the wrong axes\"\n    )\n\n\ndef test_converted_mesh_faces_the_right_way():\n    volume, affine = _synthetic_volume()\n    mask = dicom_to_mesh.segment_bone(volume, threshold_hu=300.0)\n    mesh = dicom_to_mesh.mask_to_mesh(mask, affine)\n\n    assert mesh.is_watertight\n    assert mesh.volume > 0, \"inverted normals give a negative volume\"\n\n\n# -- the PHI check ------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_phi_scan_reports_identifiers(tmp_path):\n    pydicom = pytest.importorskip(\"pydicom\", reason=\"requirements-dicom.txt not installed\")\n    from pydicom.dataset import FileDataset, FileMetaDataset\n    from pydicom.uid import CTImageStorage, ExplicitVRLittleEndian\n\n    meta = FileMetaDataset()\n    meta.MediaStorageSOPClassUID = CTImageStorage\n    meta.MediaStorageSOPInstanceUID = pydicom.uid.generate_uid()\n    meta.TransferSyntaxUID = ExplicitVRLittleEndian\n\n    ds = FileDataset(str(tmp_path / \"slice.dcm\"), {}, file_meta=meta, preamble=b\"\\0\" * 128)\n    ds.PatientName = \"Doe^Jane\"\n    ds.PatientID = \"123456\"\n    ds.save_as(str(tmp_path / \"slice.dcm\"), enforce_file_format=True)\n\n    found = dicom_to_mesh.scan_for_phi(tmp_path)\n    assert \"PatientName\" in found\n    assert \"PatientID\" in found\n\n\ndef test_phi_scan_on_a_directory_without_dicom(tmp_path):\n    pytest.importorskip(\"pydicom\", reason=\"requirements-dicom.txt not installed\")\n    (tmp_path / \"notes.txt\").write_text(\"not a scan\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    with pytest.raises(DicomError, match=\"no readable DICOM\"):\n        dicom_to_mesh.scan_for_phi(tmp_path)\n"}
